fieldMarks: White chinstrap on a black head and neck
Populations vary greatly in size and body colour, from white-chested to very dark
behavior: Flies in V-formation, northbound in spring and southbound in fall; family groups migrate together
Grazes mostly while walking on land; also feeds in water by dipping or up-ending
Many urban and refuge birds are now permanent residents
Feeds in flocks at most seasons, often in open fields in winter
habitat: Always nests near water: tundra, fresh and salt marshes, wooded lakes, and city park and suburban ponds; winters where fields for feeding are within commuting distance of water.
range: Breeds from central and southeastern Alaska across northern Canada south to southwestern British Columbia and much of the northern and central United States; resident year-round in the central part of the range, with many populations in urban areas no longer migrating.

lookalikes.name: Cackling goose
lookalikes.howToTell: The smallest forms formerly included in this species are now treated as the separate Cackling Goose; compare size closely.
